changed.what: Request from U21b honoured: doctor gained a section interface (DoctorSection trait, static table, --section, unknown section 802 with pointer) and the later sections kernels (N21b-01), ledger (N34-26) and registries (N32ax-03). The over-budget row of GATE-TETHER-03 had no estimable run verb at M0: added the test-lane overlay `synthetic-verbs` (synthetic.deferred, synthetic.estimable with a fixed estimate and the worked 701 case), excluded from release builds. The grammar unit test used design.check, which is not registered at M0: made it a synthetic entry. The component scripts of N32a-03 and N32a-04 drive `frob`, which first exists here, so they are now run green in this bead's acceptance. Added dep N32a-01 (the ADR-TETHER-01 verb-literal lint this bead asserts; also resolves the graph finding that nothing depended on N32a-01). Round two of edits: the overlay's uncalibrated interval is [0.5, 2], N32a-15's rule point/2 to point*2 (was [1, 2]).
ADR-TETHER-10's governing bead was 'the beads of the other Tether unit'; the index needs keys: named N32b-06 and N32b-10, measured by N32b-09 and N32b-14.

RL-06 required a non-empty chapter refusal list for every verb taking input, which the operator rows (refusals = []) violate: the rule now applies to the full list (chapter plus appended codes). RL-15 said the scope registry arrives at M3 with BD-258; it arrives at M2 with N32b-01 (BD-258 adds admin scopes at M3). Added the field `key_optional` and lint RL-21 for the one optional-key exemption (study.plan) that N32a-09 and N32a-13 cite but no field carried. Fixed the cluster count (243 verbs in about 44 clusters; 34 is the mechanical inventory's). RL-21 also admits session.focus (key_optional; its appended list omits 805), whose keyless calls the kind rule would otherwise refuse.

The panic envelope carried 'a 9xx integrity code' but no 9xx code exists in the refusal registry: chose FROB-REF-990 internal-fault (provisional, DESIGN, clear of the proposed 901-907 and the 999 sentinel) with retry never and repairs; request to N32-REF to enter the row. Its e2e drives `frob`, which BD-022 builds on this crate: the script is authored here and run green in BD-022; added the unit test exit_fixture_rows so the fixture is checked here.

Step 7 routed run verbs by an 'in-process limit' registry field that N32a-02's closed schema does not have, and running a run verb in a client while a daemon is up would bind its key outside the one ledger (INV-TETHER-05): routing is now a rule of kind, tier and daemon reachability, with the M0 no-ledger case stated. The conformance suite and e2e named the M0 operator verbs, which BD-022 builds on this interface: they now run a synthetic dispatch fixture through frob-rpc-serve and frob-rpc-call, and BD-022 reruns them on the operator verbs. Added test route_by_kind_and_daemon. Moved N33c-35 (the OPEN-SUITE-6 decision on Cx, which the trait signature uses) from related to deps.

The scratch-approval hold needs a job row, which does not exist until the ledger (M1) and the daemon (M2), and the bead had no path into the admission transaction: made the hold a pure function scratch_hold, stored in N32a-08's new `hold` column and written by N32a-09; at M0 a would-be-held run is refused 761 with scratch_verdict admitted. Acceptance and tests staged accordingly.

Handler fault now carries FROB-REF-990 (consistent with N32a-03). The smoke test required doctor to exit 0, which fails on a host with an absent device: 0 or 2, equal to the CLI's. definition_from_entry used sim.run and an admin entry that are not in this bead's dependencies: synthetic entries; added handler_fault_990.

kill_mcp_decision.sh diffed the tool list against `frob schema --list`, which no bead defines: now against `frob capabilities --json`. Named the M0 verb-serving loop (frob-rpc-serve) for the rehearsal and added failure details to its log.
Log lines lacked the evidence block, the asupersync count per workspace and failure details; added.
Schema file path was the rejected `registries/schemas/frob.common@1.json`; now schemas/frob.common.1.json per N32a-02. Out-of-range int53 emission is FROB-REF-990 with a test.

Added the `hold` column and the held-job rule (never started by queue or recovery; only admitted to cancelled), which N32ax-03's scratch-approval hold needs and no table carried; test held_job_never_starts.

The admission transaction now writes the scratch hold (N32ax-03's scratch_hold with N36-20's needed class); deps N32ax-03 and N36-20 added. The optional-key exemption names its registry field key_optional and lint RL-21. Tests scratch_hold_set_in_transaction and key_optional_content_addressed.

e2e used `frob job find --key` (the reconciled form is --verb and --key) and the verb job.find is registered by N29a-23, which depends on this bead: that step is logged skipped until then and the lookup is asserted by the new unit test restart_then_find_by_key. The queue never dequeues a held job; test held_job_never_dequeued.

The live-pin cap had no number: 256 per principal, LRU expiry to 807, with a test. The e2e paged `telemetry.query`, whose verb bead (N24a-36) does not depend on this one: the script now pages a synthetic paginated verb from BD-022's test overlay and is parameterized so BD-211 reruns it on telemetry.query and job.list (dep BD-022 added); evidence block added to the log.

module.list, module.show and module.check are built by N15b-02, which nothing in the M1 capstone's dependency set reached (the only M1 verb bead missing from it): added the dep and named it in the cluster table. The checklist used the field `when`; the registry's spelling is `use_when` (N32a-02), and a run entry also needs its `wait` table.

session.focus is a mutate verb, so the kind rule (RL-08) would make the generator require an idempotency key and refuse every `session_focus {cluster}` call, including all of the plan's worked session, with 805: the row is now key_optional under RL-21 (a set-to-value change of the caller's own session). Clarified that the refusal column shows appended codes. Test focus_needs_no_key.
Acceptance called verb_invoke one of four allowlisted non-registry tools; the other three allowlisted names are the base tools, which are registry verbs (N32a-11).

The PairCounts integrity fault had no code: FROB-REF-990 (exit 9). The optional key on study.plan is now one of the two RL-21 cases (with session.focus). study.cancel is first due at M2 in the appendix and lands here at M3: stated that it answers 724 at M2 and that a study is cancelled through job.cancel on its job meanwhile.

The registry lint 'estimable on every verb whose cost model can exceed one second' had no owner or decidable rule, and BD-222's negative control relies on it: defined lint `estimate-required` here (estimable iff the cost model has the `estimated:` form; every job-submitting run verb estimable; a static bound above 1 s is a warning, design.check at M2), with a test.

The wait table was spelled `{ cli = "complete", mcp_default_ms, max_ms }`, the draft N32a-02 replaced; now `{ cli = "to-completion", mcp_ms, mcp_max_ms }`. job.wait is a read verb that takes sync_wait_ms, contradicting 'read verbs do not accept it': stated as its own input property, with no wait table (RL-18).
A progress regression was 'an integrity fault' with no code or outcome: the frame is dropped, the job untouched, the wait ends with FROB-REF-990 and the job-find repair.

A1 read the chunk index through 'telemetry query (or the store's audit read verb)'; no verb exposes the raw chunk index: A1 is the conformance frontier audit over a ledger copy, cross-checked from the user's side by telemetry.query.

The code-to-exit check runs at M2 while the refusal beads of §26, §39 (M3) and §31 (M5) land later: stated that it is a standing per-commit test and BD-299 records it with them. Added 990 to the family-default test.
Acceptance asserted the hysteresis band and a tested KILL-PREEMPT configuration with no unit test for either: added hysteresis_enter_10_leave_5 and preempt_disabled_config.

The oversize resource read had no code and the bead 'blocked on this point'; N32-REF assigns FROB-REF-838 (provisional): used it with its payload and repairs. The schema URI example used the rejected `@` form; schema ids in a URI are written with `/` as `.`.

Its identifier pattern differed from the one N32b-18 owns as data (no `/`): now N32b-18's. The seven workflow files were attributed to BD-313, which depends on this bead, while this bead's tests need them: their step form is written here, BD-313 builds the full sessions on them. Stated the omission rule both renderings share so prompt and robot-docs stay equal in every build; tests added.

Read KILL-SOLVE's clause 1 (the paper ceiling) after the verb it gates had been built (it depends on BD-372), while BD-372 was gated only on the pilot's own verdict; the decision's stricter conservative recount could then fire after the work was spent. Clause 1 moved to the new decision bead N32ap1-01 between the pilot and BD-372; this bead keeps clause 2 and completes the same ADR and row.

Now depends on the clause-1 decision N32ap1-01 and is closed as not built on its `fired: ceiling` entry. Its registry row is VERBS-solve's (dep added; no second copy): the row declares `solve:run`, where this bead listed opt:run, sim:run, study:submit as the row's capabilities; those are now checked as the called verbs' scopes before any job (720 naming the missing scope). Out names the A/B bead (BD-374) and both decision beads. Tests called_scopes_checked_first and campaign_class_704 (the campaign-class refusal is named).
The wait table used the replaced spelling; per-verb override is `wait.mcp_ms` (N32a-02); the schema read is `frob schema sim.run --in --json`.
The count of further conditions disagreed with the four listed; the default was ambiguous: it stays blocked unless the decision reads `build`, standalone machines being the intended default.

The peer link had no kill gate, though it forwards jobs between machines: added KILL-PEERLINK (triggers: a double admission or charge; a forbidden-class or private byte on the wire; recovered device time below 10% over 4 weeks; fallback standalone), with acceptance, test kill_peerlink_decision and the log summary. A forwarded job introduced a ninth job state the 8-state ledger does not have: the row stays `running` with `forwarded_to` and `peer_job` columns; test forwarded_job_keeps_eight_states. Out names N32a-34 and N41-12.
e2e used job find without the verb; now `frob job find --verb sim.run --key k2`; dep N29a-23 (the job.find verb) added.

Acceptance used `frob job find --key <k>`; a key is scoped to principal and verb: now --verb and --key. The e2e now reruns N32a-10's pagination script on telemetry.query and job.list, which N32a-10 hands to this bead and nothing ran. Deps N24a-36 (telemetry.query) and N29a-23 (the job verbs) added; no cycle.

Its daemon-era common codes by kind were a shorter second list (no 704, 723, 808; 720 only once tokens exist) where BD-137 and NJL-01 have one rule: now the same appended sets, with test appended_refusals_one_rule. telemetry.inspect-pixel and export-html are built by N24a-40 and N24a-41, not BD-191: deps added. study.cancel is registered declared (724) until N32a-13 at M3; test study_cancel_declared_at_m2. The task-cluster assignment is NJL-05's; this bead checks it. The estimable rule cites N32a-15's lint.
Acceptance required 'the pilot for slot dispatch' without naming it: N21b-20 (a dependency), with its queue trace, ceiling and falsifier and a funding verdict.
The not-fired branch named the mode `--dispatch=slots`; BD-295's modes are per-job, shadow and shared: now `--dispatch=shared`.
The deficit round-robin increment q0 was undefined: the scheduling quantum (5 s default, OPEN-TETHER-4), the one N32a-21 measures the deficit against.

Claimed 'the complete task-cluster assignment' and carried its own starting assignment of eleven further clusters, a second table beside NJL-05's 45-cluster assignment (a dependency) against which the every-verb-seated lint is checked: the assignment and its lints are NJL-05's; this bead checks the served surface (M-focus) and keeps no list. Acceptance reworded to the served-surface check.

The handler-fault skeleton had no code: FROB-REF-990 (N32a-03), retry never, job-find repair. The by-kind 805 stimulus would fail the key_optional rows (session.focus, study.plan): excepted, with test key_optional_rows_skip_805. Recovery used job.find by key alone: now by verb and key. Recorded N32a-19's hand-off: the M3 code-to-exit reading lists the chapters present (§26, §39 now) and names §31 absent. The sealed-read row in Considerations had no test or acceptance: added sealed_read_refusal_reveals_no_world.

Same refusal-set drift as BD-222 (a shorter list by kind): now the one rule of NJL-01/BD-137, test appended_refusals_one_rule. Sealed-read refusal named FROB-REF-840 (N39-REF). Task-cluster assignment deferred to NJL-05 (dep). Estimable rule cites N32a-15 (dep). declared_verbs_724 covers shield.check too. Dependency count corrected (about sixty).

The guide's recovery text named job.find without the verb. The step form of the workflow files is N32a-26's (now a direct dep): this bead adds the sessions' commands and keeps steps equal, test worked_sessions_follow_workflow_files.

Named the two KILL-SOLVE decision beads (clause 1 N32ap1-01, final N32a-32) and the not-run case of the second arm. The bead runs the fresh agent 'only on a build where session_mission.sh passes' but nothing checked it: the e2e now runs that script first and the record cites it.

Depended on N32a-32 (the final KILL-SOLVE status, after the A/B) while its freeze rule allows the decision to be pending: now depends on the clause-1 decision N32ap1-01, N32a-32 related. When clause 1 fires, solve_run leaves `search` with six tools (NJL-05's rule; its `opt_cascade` proposal is requested of NJL-05). 'All eight conditions' spelled out. Sealed read named 840. Assignment deferred to NJL-05 (dep).

Proposed two clusters of its own (`reality-2`, `make-2`) for verbs NJL-05 already seats (calibrate, structure, proofs, places-check): withdrawn in favour of NJL-05 (dep), test m5_verbs_seated_per_njl05. new_beads.why: split from N32a-32: KILL-SOLVE's clause 1 must be decided between the pilot (N32a-31) and the verb (BD-372), not after the verb is built

requests.what: Enter FROB-REF-990 `internal-fault` (provisional number, family 9xx internal per BD-005): a handler panicked or returned an unhandled error, or a serializer refused an out-of-range int53; exit 9; retry never; repairs (1) `frob job find --verb <verb> --key <key>` when the call carried a key, (2) `frob doctor`; the diagnostic file path in `observed`. N32a-03, BD-022, BD-023 and N32a-07 raise it.

Under a scratch registries root (N32ax-03) admission still decides from the scratch registry, but a job needing more than the class in force of record is held (from M1: admitted with hold scratch-approval, never started; at M0: refused 761 with scratch_verdict admitted). The acceptance line 'approving E1 in a scratch registry admits it' should assert the decision and the hold, and zero worlds stepped.

telemetry.query should be wired through N32a-10's Paginated wrapper and depend on N32a-10: a cursor reused with a changed filter, order or pin answers FROB-REF-806 at the surface (the plan's §32.8.1 code) with FROB-REF-896 as its cause, not a bare 896; the response's cursor is the authenticated frob.cursor/1.

BD-022 gives `doctor` the input `--section <name>` (sections toolchain, stack, stack_receipt, upstream, devices, kernel_cache, probes, daemon, plus kernels, ledger, registries from later beads) and `capabilities` the filters `--verb`, `--device`; the rows list both verbs' inputs as none.

session.focus: set `key_optional = true` (N32a-02 RL-21 now admits it: a set-to-value change of the caller's own session; the plan's worked session calls session_focus with no key, which RL-08 would refuse with 805). Its appended refusal list then omits 805.

If KILL-SOLVE's clause 1 fires (N32ap1-01), remove the solve.run row before the M4 freeze in the same change (solve_run then leaves `search`, NJL-05). 'Implemented by: BD-372, N32a-32' should read 'implemented by BD-372; decided by N32ap1-01 (clause 1) and N32a-32 (clause 2)'. The row's capability `solve:run` stands; BD-372 additionally checks the called verbs' scopes (opt:run, sim:run, study:submit, qual:run when stop_at = qualify) and refuses 720 before any job; the row's description may say so.

Add the KILL-PEERLINK row to the kill-gate register (N32a-35): triggers (a) a double admission or double charge of a forwarded job, (b) a forbidden-class or private byte on the wire, (c) recovered device time below 10% over a four-week reading; fallback: standalone machines; read at the end of the four weeks.
Name KILL-PEERLINK (N32a-35) as the gate whose recorded pass enables `fleet.peer_link = true`; until then the default is standalone.

design.check's cost model is `static: under 2 s`, which N32a-15's new lint estimate-required reports as a warning (a static bound above 1 s): add an `estimated:` cost model or tighten the static bound to at most 1 s.

BD-376 had proposed seating `opt_cascade` in `search` when KILL-SOLVE fires; it now follows NJL-05's rule (six tools). Decide whether `opt_cascade` should take the vacated seat and, if so, state it in the KILL-SOLVE line of the assignment.

notes: All 56 beads of the slice reviewed against the plan and the brief. Cross-cutting reconciliations: the job-find form (--verb and --key) everywhere; FROB-REF-990 for internal faults; the wait table spelled per N32a-02; one appended refusal rule per kind (BD-222, BD-312 had shorter lists); task-cluster assignment owned by NJL-05 only (BD-298, BD-312, BD-376, BD-409 had second tables); KILL-SOLVE split so clause 1 (new N32ap1-01) sits between the pilot and BD-372; KILL-PEERLINK added in N32a-35. coverage.md updated for N32ap1-01 and KILL-PEERLINK. graph_check: 0 cycles. The slice looks settled pending the listed requests.
